# Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS) index

Every OEIS A-number cited on this wiki or listed in its sequence data (354 sequences, cited on 162 pages) and where it appears. Use it to find where an A-number is discussed. A-numbers link to OEIS. "Pages" lists the wiki pages that mention the number, most mentions first, with the mention count in parentheses; the primary discussion is generally the page with the highest count.

This page and [[castle-sequence-catalog](pages/castle-sequence-catalog.md)] are generated by `bin/generate-sequence-pages.py` from one data file, `config/castle-sequences.tsv`. The castle role of each entry is built from the rows that name it; the catalog shows the same rows by family, with their terms. The method for identifying and verifying an OEIS match is on [[oeis-cross-referencing](pages/oeis-cross-referencing.md)].

Every 2 × 2 square of cells in this castle rests on the bottom row, the group is cyclic, and its order is the even-indexed Fibonacci number `F_{2w}`; it is a statistic of one castle for each `w` (`w = 1…`): `A001906(w)`; the even-indexed Fibonacci numbers `F_{2n}`. | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) | a(0) = 0, a(1) = a(2) = a(3) = 1; thereafter, a(n) = a(n-1) + a(n-2) + a(n-4). | the number of tree castles of area `n`, the number of cells, with the height unrestricted: castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2, which is exactly when the castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) is a tree ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)], [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]). Read left to right, the column heights of a tree castle are a composition of `n` (an ordered sum of positive parts) with no two neighboring parts at least 2, and every such composition is a tree castle (`n = 1…`): `A005251(n+2)`; the number of binary strings of length `N` with no factor `010`, that is, no three consecutive symbols `0, 1, 0`. These strings are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the gap map writes a tree castle of area `n` as a string of length `N = n − 1`, each column of height `c` becoming `c − 1` zeros and neighboring columns separated by a single `1`, and it is a bijection from the tree castles of area `n` onto these strings ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) (`N = 0…`): `A005251(N+3)`; the number `W_1(N)` of binary words of length `N` with no isolated `1`, so that every run of 1s has length at least 2. `W_1` is the case `m = 1` of the words `W_m` of [[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)] (words in `{0, …, m}^N` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors), whose cases `m = 2, 3, 4` are Hardin's OEIS entries. The words are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the column map sends a tree castle of area `n` to a word of length `N = n`, a column of height 1 becoming `0` and a column of height `c ≥ 2` becoming `1^c`, one-to-one and onto ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]) (`N = 1…`): `A005251(N+2)`; the number of compositions of `m` (ordered ways of writing `m` as a sum of positive parts) with no part equal to 2. They are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the leading-column map puts a column of height 1 in front of a tree castle of area `n` and merges each column of height 1 followed by a column of height `j ≥ 2` into one part `1 + j`, which gives a composition of `m = n + 1` with no part 2, one-to-one and onto ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]) (`m = 1…`): `A005251(m+1)`; the number of skylines of width `w` with every column between 1 and 2 and tower spacing at least 2: in every row, each run of empty cells that has filled cells on both sides is at least 2 columns wide ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). Such a skyline need not reach height 2, so this counts the castles of width `w` and of every height up to 2 with that spacing; the castles of height exactly 2 among them number this count minus 1, the flat row `(1, …, 1)`. The gap map followed by the complement carries the tree castles of area `w + 1` (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) one to one onto these skylines ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) (`w = 1…`): `A005251(w+3)`; the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 6 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, written `P_even(6, L)` (the even sector of the signed tower count), divided by `2^L`; a tower being what remains of a castle when its bottom row, which is one block, is removed: `L` columns of heights 0 to 6, all of height 0 allowed ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)], [[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)]). It is a signed sum, and it equals a count: `P_even(6, L) = 2^L W_1(L + 1)`, with `W_1(N)` the number of binary strings of length `N` with no isolated 1, so the quotient is the number of tree castles of area `L + 1` (castles with no two neighboring columns both of height at least 2), proved by a change of basis between transfer matrices ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)], [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) (`L = 0…`): `A005251(L+3)`; the number of skylines of width `w` with every column between 1 and 2 and tower spacing at least 2: in every row, each run of empty cells that has filled cells on both sides is at least 2 columns wide ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). Such a skyline need not reach height 2, so this counts the castles of width `w` and of every height up to 2 with that spacing; the castles of height exactly 2 among them number this count minus 1, the flat row `(1, …, 1)` (`w = 1…`): `A005251(w+3)` | [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)] (37), [[castle-snippets-strips](pages/castle-snippets-strips.md)] (23), [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)] (17), [[plastic-number](pages/plastic-number.md)] (9), [[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)] (8), [[hardin-identity-seminar](pages/hardin-identity-seminar.md)] (8), [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] (7), [[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)] (7), [[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)] (6), [[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)] (4), [[n-nacci-disambiguation](pages/n-nacci-disambiguation.md)] (4), [[castle-snippets](pages/castle-snippets.md)] (3), [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)] (3), [[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)] (3), [[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)] (1), [[castle-classification-growth](pages/castle-classification-growth.md)] (1), [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)] (1), [[castle-classification-spectrum](pages/castle-classification-spectrum.md)] (1), [[castle-snippets-number-theory](pages/castle-snippets-number-theory.md)] (1), [[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)] (1), [[q-thread-seminar](pages/q-thread-seminar.md)] (1) |

At `j = 1` this is the total number of height-1 columns, `A045623(n − 1)`; since a castle with `k` height-1 columns has `k + 1` prime factors (the pieces left by cutting it at its height-1 columns, [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]), a castle of area `n ≥ 2` has `(n + 6)/4` prime factors on average | [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)] (6), [[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)] (5) |
